verdict.rationale: 1Password's SDKs explicitly offer programmatic item management. The CLI, Connect REST API and Service Accounts provide documented machine surfaces for vault items, so an agent can plausibly store credentials. The evidence never shows explicit create or update operations, and storing one-time passwords is documented only as a user-app feature. missing for 10: explicit documented create/update item calls (the CLI reference shown only covers `op item list`), programmatic TOTP-secret seeding, confirmation that Connect/Service Accounts allow writes, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can create and update vault entries — seeding new TOTP secrets, storing credentials — through documented programmatic surfaces

citations.quote: Automate item management: Programmatically manage items in your 1Password account.
1Password SDKs allow you to build integrations that programmatically interact with 1Password using Go, JavaScript, or Python.
1Password Connect Servers allow you to securely access your 1Password items and vaults in your company's apps and cloud infrastructure using a private REST API.
1Password Service Accounts help automate secrets management in your applications and infrastructure
